title: Autocalib: stratified cohort harness for FP8/INT8 acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated validation harness that accepts or rejects a quantized model variant (FP8/INT8 profiles) using stratified cohorts of canonical prompts, multi-metric assertions, and adaptive pass/fail gates. This ticket scopes the implementation of the harness, instrumentation requirements, canary integration, and CI gating rules. The goal is a deterministic, reproducible pipeline that produces an acceptance decision and a human-readable report (diffs, sample failures, metric time series) to surface regressions early in rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end in CI and emits a single PASS/FAIL decision artifact
Stratified cohorts cover: short conversational prompts, long-form instructions, code completions, and domain-specific templates (finance, healthcare)
Metrics computed: semantic similarity (SBERT cosine), token edit distance, logit-rank correlation, KS test on token distributions, and response-length shift
Adaptive thresholds use historical baseline and beta-prior smoothing to avoid noisy rejections on small cohorts
Failing examples are saved to S3 and linked in the report along with nearest-matching golden response and diff
CI blocks merges on FAIL for runtime-1.22 branch and opens a diagnostic issue with links to telemetry dashboards
implementation_notes: Use stratified reservoir sampling to keep cohort sizes bounded while preserving rare-domain examples
Golden corpus will be stored as canonical seeds (anchor prompts) with one or more curated reference responses per prompt
For semantic similarity use SBERT encodings with cosine similarity aggregated by cohort median and 10th percentile
Compute logit-rank correlation by comparing top-5 token rank ordering between float baseline and quantized variant
Apply KS test to token probability distributions over a sliding window of tokens (to detect subtle distributional drift)
Report includes waterfall of metric deltas, per-prompt scatter, and an aggregated risk score used by the gate
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We debated fixed thresholds vs adaptive: adaptive chosen to reduce false positives during low-sample cohorts
Semantic similarity is expensive; we'll precompute embeddings for goldens and only embed candidate outputs in the harness
Per-prompt exact-match is too brittle for instruction-style outputs; use token-edit distance + semantic similarity instead
We will not block on running the full data-parallel sim tests in CI initially; the harness will run a representative stratified subset with a follow-up nightly full-run
risks: Cohort selection bias could hide regressions in unrepresented business-critical prompts
Embedding drift over time may shift SBERT baselines; requires periodic refresh of golden encodings
Telemetry overload: naive collection of token-level distributions can create high cardinality metrics
Model nondeterminism for sampling-based decoders can increase noise; we will run deterministic decoding for acceptance tests
plan: Week 1: implement harness scaffolding, CI integration, and storage schema for goldens and failures
Week 2: implement metrics (SBERT, edit-distance, logit-rank, KS test) and initial cohort definitions
Week 3: run shadow canaries against recent quantized profiles, collect baseline history, tune adaptive thresholds
Week 4: lock rule set, add human readable reporting and Dashboard panels, flip to block-on-fail for runtime-1.22
